overview.text: Colombia, officially the Republic of Colombia, occupies the northwestern corner of South America; its capital, Bogotá, stands high in the Andes. The country is especially varied in landforms: geographers distinguish six natural regions—Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, Orinoquía, Amazonian, and Insular. In the west, the Andes divide into three cordilleras, with the Cauca and Magdalena river valleys between them. Northern lowlands reach the Caribbean, while the Pacific region lies to the west; broad plains and savannas extend east toward Amazonian rainforest. These sharp contrasts in elevation and landscape help make Colombia’s geography distinctive, from mountain valleys and highlands to tropical coasts and forests.

key_facts.text: Colombia lies in the northwestern corner of South America.
Bogotá is the country’s capital, located in the Andes at about 2,600 meters above sea level.
Colombia’s six natural regions are Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, Orinoquía, Amazonian, and Insular.
In Colombia, the Andes form three cordilleras separated by the Cauca and Magdalena river valleys.
The eastern Orinoquía is characterized by plains and savannas, while the Amazonian region includes rainforest.
